name: Detect configuration drift continuously and bound temporary changes
description: Make deviation from the baseline detectable while it is happening rather than at review time, and give temporary rules an owner and an expiry so their closure does not depend on recollection.

steps.action: Enable continuous comparison of live configuration against the reviewed baseline, alerting on deviation.
Route drift alerts to a named owner with a defined response timeframe, so detection produces action.
Record both detection time and resolution time for every deviation, so drift duration is measurable.
Require temporary rules to carry an owner and an expiry, and expire them automatically where the platform allows.
Extend configuration change history retention to at least the examination period plus a margin.
Schedule dated configuration captures as a fallback where a platform provides no native change history.

implementation_considerations: Retention is the step most often overlooked and the one that silently invalidates everything else; check the default retention of every audit log being relied on before assuming coverage.
Drift alerting is noisy at first because the baseline is usually wrong in small ways. Budget a tuning period rather than disabling it when the volume arrives.
Where infrastructure is already defined as code with full repository history, much of this exists; the gap is usually detection of out-of-band changes made directly in the console.
This remediation serves every control that relies on point-in-time configuration evidence, not only the boundary. Scope it once across identity, encryption, and network surfaces.
typical_duration: Weeks to deploy; one full period to accumulate the coverage it exists to provide.
prerequisites: An approved baseline to compare against, from REM-NETSEC-001
Platform audit logging enabled with adequate retention

verification_method.how: Confirm change history spans the intended period, that a deliberately introduced test deviation is detected and alerted, and that detection and resolution times are both recorded.

residual_risk_note: Drift detection reduces the window during which a deviation goes unnoticed; it does not prevent the deviation. Preventive controls over who can change the boundary remain necessary.
period_limitation_note: Coverage begins when the mechanism is switched on. It cannot reconstruct history for a period already elapsed, so an entity that starts this mid-period will still have an unevidenced interval.
notes: This is the structural answer to the point-in-time versus period evidence problem across CC6, and is the companion to EV-CONFIG-001.
